Maya (People Ops): Quick update 1 1 two small policy changes + a mandatory reminder.

1) Family Care Leave consolidation: starting June 1 we
re consolidating short-term family care (sick child, elder care) into a single 10-day annual bank called "Family Care". Unused days do not carry over. Applies globally but amount may vary by local law; see doc.

2) Travel reimbursement cap update: standard meal per diem cap increased to $75/day for US and CAD trips; rest of world uses local per-diem table linked in policy. Submit receipts within 30 days.

Mandatory: Code of Conduct refresher 1 All employees must complete the 10-min Code of Conduct micro-training by May 20. Completion is tracked in LMS; managers will get a compliance report. If you need accommodations email people-ops@redwood.com.

hr-bot: Policy docs updated: https://redwood.internal/hr/policies/family-care-2026 and https://redwood.internal/hr/policies/travel-2026. Training link: https://lms.redwood.internal/coc-2026

Tom: If I
lready took a single-day caregiver day in May, does it come out of the new bank?

Maya (People Ops): Days taken before June 1 remain unchanged. New bank applies to absences from June 1 onward.

Aisha K.: Will managers see Family Care usage on the HR portal?

hr-bot: Yes, usage appears on the Time Off page; privacy notes are respected (reason shown as Family Care, not specific details).

Legal-Bot: For teams in EMEA check local laws in the doc; some countries require carryover, in which case policy defaults to local law.

Maya (People Ops): Office hours Friday 4pm PT in #people-ops-office-hours for Qs. Thanks! :seedling:
